sources.title: Ex Post Evaluation #6: Climate Change Adaptation Programme in Water and Agriculture in Anseba Region, Eritrea
sources.organization: Adaptation Fund Technical Evaluation Reference Group; evaluation conducted by Universalia Management Group
sources.temporal_coverage: AF-supported project outcomes seven years after its 2018 closure; fieldwork in August 2025.
sources.methodology: Independent AF-TERG ex-post evaluation using document review, interviews, focus groups, transect walks, observation and site visits.
sources.limitations: Eight of 16 project sites were visited; findings are not a region-wide census.

sources.title: Returning Thirsty: Water Supply, Livelihoods and Returnees in the Gash-Barka Region, Eritrea
sources.organization: Overseas Development Institute, South Bank University and Eritrean research collaborators
sources.temporal_coverage: Post-border-war return and resettlement period; field research around 2001 and report published in 2002.
sources.methodology: Field research in nine Gash-Barka communities using rapid appraisal, interviews and a structured 156-household survey.
sources.limitations: Historical post-conflict study; reports localized resource tensions, not climate-caused or widespread armed violence.

sources.title: Climate Change Adaptation Programme in Water and Agriculture in Anseba Region, Eritrea: Eritrea Case Study
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme Adaptation Learning Mechanism
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical climate and livelihood conditions reported for a 2012 project case study, including 2002–2004 rainfall impacts.
sources.methodology: UNDP case study presents local climate, livelihood and water context for an adaptation programme and its design.
sources.limitations: Project-preparation context, not a current reassessment or outcome evaluation; projections and conditions are dated.

sources.title: Climate Risks and Adaptation Guidelines for Power Transmission and Solar Generation Systems in the Sahel Region: Country Chapter – Eritrea
sources.temporal_coverage: Reference climatology 1961–1990, historical climate 1990–2020 and projections for 2030–2060.
sources.methodology: Country chapter summarizes modelled hazards and risks to solar technologies, drawing on GCA's 2022 Sahel hazard assessment.
sources.limitations: High-level, energy-asset assessment; the report calls for site-specific studies and notes climate-model uncertainty.

claims.paraphrase: At five consulted project sites, dams, diversions and water-harvesting structures still supported irrigation, pastoralism and hygiene; siltation and maintenance problems limited sustainability.
claims.limitations: Selected visited sites, not region-wide coverage.

claims.locator: Printed p. 3, Outcome 2 findings and regional-authority data
claims.paraphrase: Ministry-led MIHAP replication sustained agricultural diversification and livestock production; Anseba authorities reported 58 of 640 participating households became small or medium commercial enterprises.
claims.limitations: The 640-household figure is from regional authorities; some benefits were beneficiary-reported.

claims.paraphrase: Three of six hydromet stations observed generated data, but two partly functioned; data were not centrally automated and only some farmers received extension advice.
claims.limitations: Evaluation snapshot; three stations were directly observed.

claims.locator: Printed p. 5, contribution to local resilience
claims.paraphrase: The evaluation found women’s participation and leadership sustained after the project; women reported reduced water-fetching burdens, and children’s school attendance improved.
claims.limitations: Some effects are stakeholder-reported; project sites only.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 24–25, returnee impacts perceived by Goluj residents
claims.paraphrase: After the border war disrupted transhumance and Tekezze-Setit basin watering access, herds shifted to wells around Goluj and nearby return sites; the study reports emerging farmer–livestock-owner conflict.
claims.limitations: Localized post-war tensions in 1999–2001; not evidence of climate-caused or widespread armed conflict.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: ODI attributes peak livestock pressure to war-disrupted herding routes and reports emerging farmer–livestock-owner conflict near Goluj.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 1–2, executive-summary findings on returnee water provision and resource use
claims.paraphrase: Rapid borehole development in Gash-Barka changed water use and encouraged larger livestock populations; the study cautioned that resource pressure could threaten poor returnee and stayee livelihoods.
claims.limitations: Historical findings and future concerns; resource degradation is not attributed to climate change.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 20–21, fuelwood availability, access and household response
claims.paraphrase: Around Goluj, respondents linked scarcer fuelwood to population-related forest depletion; poor households lacking transport or money reduced use, while animal owners could access markets.
claims.limitations: Historical household survey and interviews; findings concern sampled communities.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 2–3 (one-based), Anseba climate and livelihood context
claims.paraphrase: UNDP’s case study reports erratic below-average rain in 2002–2004, especially in parts of Habero, caused livestock losses and impaired livelihoods; annual rain ranged from 190 mm in Habero to about 367 mm in Hamelmalo.
claims.limitations: Historical project-preparation context, not a recent rainfall assessment.

claims.locator: PDF p. 2 (one-based), Anseba pastoral movements and land-use context
claims.paraphrase: Anseba herders moved west in July–September and toward the eastern escarpment or Northern Red Sea in November–March; land-use pressure, degradation and settlement policies disrupted this practice.
claims.limitations: The case study lists multiple pressures and policies; it does not isolate their effects.

claims.paraphrase: For solar-asset planning, GCA describes lowland and coastal rainfall below 100 mm with dry spells over 200 days, versus wetter highlands; drought hazard is very high across most Eritrea and dust/wind risk is elevated in Anseba.
claims.limitations: GCA summarizes modelled climatology and high-level asset hazards, not local household impacts.

claims.paraphrase: For 2030–2060, mean annual rainfall is projected to fall by up to 100 mm on the Eritrean Plateau, with slight increases in western lowlands and southern areas; wet-day changes are small under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5.
claims.limitations: The source notes high climate-model uncertainty; the chapter is not a general social-risk assessment.

search_audit.query: Eritrea Anseba Habero drought livestock climate vulnerability local adaptation evaluation report
search_audit.outcome: AF-TERG evaluation and UNDP case study provide named Anseba sites and differentiated drought, water and livelihood findings; GCA adds regional hazard differentiation for energy assets.

search_audit.query: Eritrea climate drought water conflict livelihoods displacement returnees Gash Barka
search_audit.outcome: The historical ODI field study documents border-war disruption of herding routes, local water pressure and emerging farmer–livestock-owner disputes; no inspected source establishes climate-caused armed conflict.

search_audit.query: Eritrea border war displacement transhumance water access returnees adaptation constraints Gash Barka
search_audit.outcome: ODI describes how border-war route restrictions and displacement shaped water access, resettlement and livestock pressure in Gash-Barka; no inspected recent source documents insecurity obstructing current adaptation delivery.

search_audit.query: Eritrea Anseba post-project adaptation resilience water infrastructure hydromet agriculture evaluation
search_audit.outcome: The 2026 ex-post evaluation reports sustained water, livelihood and women’s participation outcomes alongside maintenance and hydromet gaps; UNDP’s 2012 case study describes planned local adaptation measures.

gaps: No inspected current source establishes climate-caused armed conflict in Eritrea or current insecurity blocking adaptation. The ODI conflict and displacement findings are historical; the baseline project proposal describes water/resource conflict only as a prospective risk.
The AF-TERG evaluation visited eight of 16 project sites and is not a national or district-wide vulnerability survey.
AfDB’s 2025 WASH adaptation document listing returned HTTP 402, so its regional ESIAs and stakeholder plan could not be checked.
The GCA hazard chapter concerns solar and power assets and uses high-level climate modelling; it does not measure household or livelihood exposure.
